name: IDEAS - Imaging Database for Epilepsy And Surgery (release I: T1w/FLAIR, resection masks, outcomes)
id: OpenNeuro ds005602 (v1.0.0; raw T1w/FLAIR only) + figshare derivatives linked from cnnp-lab.com/ideas-data; DOI 10.18112/openneuro.ds005602.v1.0.0
annotations: Outcome, Resection mask, Lateralization, Clinical data
access_details: open - OpenNeuro hosts raw BIDS T1w/FLAIR; resection masks, FreeSurfer outputs and clinical metadata are on figshare via private-share links (no registration) listed on cnnp-lab.com/ideas-data; JISCmail list for updates
quality_note: Largest open pre/post-surgical epilepsy MRI cohort with resection masks, long-term ILAE outcomes, pathology and healthy controls; defaced, curated, openly licensed. Limits: single center/scanner family, dates and ages binned, outcome coarse after 5 y, FLAIR count inconsistent in paper (411 vs 420).
relevance: Directly matches surgical-outcome + resection-mask needs: combine with IDEAS II DWI (ds007401) to compute tract disconnection by resection and relate to ILAE outcome; also normative-modeling reference (BrainMoNoCle).
same_subject_data: Pre-op T1/FLAIR + resection mask from post-op imaging + post-op outcomes in same patients; IDs align with IDEAS II diffusion release (ds007401).
population: Adults (age at surgery median 37, min 16; ages binned) with drug-refractory focal epilepsy who underwent resective surgery at UCL/NHNN Queen Square (Newcastle/UCL group; Duncan). Mostly TLE (356 TLE and 58 frontal resections in mask set).
paper: Taylor PN, 2025, Epilepsia 66(2):471-481, doi:10.1111/epi.18192 (arXiv 2406.06731); resection masks: Simpson C, 2025, Imaging Neuroscience 3:IMAG.a.147, doi:10.1162/IMAG.a.147
format: BIDS NIfTI + JSON (OpenNeuro); figshare zips/tables (csv/xlsx), FreeSurfer dirs, masks in NIfTI/mgz
size: ~4.1 GB on OpenNeuro (raw T1/FLAIR); figshare derivatives additional
check_note: OpenNeuro snapshot 1.0.0 holds T1/FLAIR for 542 subjects (442 patients + 100 controls); no participants.tsv, the clinical table is on figshare.
check_changes: added tags Clinical data
confirmed_in_files: IDEAS I: raw T1/FLAIR on OpenNeuro; masks, FreeSurfer outputs and the clinical table on figshare. (checked 12 Oct 2026)

name: IDEAS II - open diffusion MRI and structural connectivity for epilepsy and surgery
id: OpenNeuro ds007401 (v1.0.0; raw DWI+T1w+FLAIR) + figshare processed DWI/connectomes; DOI 10.18112/openneuro.ds007401.v1.0.0
annotations: Outcome, Resection mask, Lateralization, Pathology, Clinical data
access_details: open - raw BIDS on OpenNeuro; processed DWI, connectomes, masks, metadata on figshare private-share links (no registration) from cnnp-lab.com/ideas-data
quality_note: Only large open epilepsy DWI release with matched controls, ready-made connectomes, resection masks and long-term seizure outcomes. Limits: single center, no iEEG/SEEG, acquisition heterogeneity across protocols, subset (216/442) of IDEAS I patients have DWI.
relevance: Core resource for white-matter/tractography work: compute resection-tract overlap and disconnectome, link to ILAE outcome; pair with public iEEG datasets only through other cohorts (no same-subject iEEG).
same_subject_data: DWI + T1/FLAIR + resection masks + surgical outcomes in the same patients (subject IDs identical to IDEAS I). No iEEG.
population: Adults with drug-refractory focal epilepsy (mostly TLE) who had resective surgery, plus controls scanned on same scanners; single UK center (Queen Square/UCL).
paper: Taylor PN, 2026, Epilepsia (in press at time of OpenNeuro release), doi:10.1002/epi.70186 (DOI as listed on cnnp-lab.com; arXiv 2602.09852)
format: BIDS NIfTI + bval/bvec + JSON; connectome matrices and tables on figshare
size: ~20.5 GB on OpenNeuro (raw); processed versions on figshare are larger
check_note: OpenNeuro snapshot 1.0.0 holds 542 subjects: T1/FLAIR for 541 and DWI for 314 (216 patients + 98 controls); no participants.tsv, the clinical table is on figshare.
check_changes: added tags Pathology, Clinical data
confirmed_in_files: IDEAS II: connectomes for 191 patients and 97 controls (Lausanne multiscale; count, FA, MD and length weights), resection masks, percent resected per region; clinical table (binned ages, FBTCS, pathology, ILAE at 1-5 years) on figshare. (checked 12 Oct 2026)

name: PennEPI collection - 103 single-subject intracranial epilepsy BIDS datasets (Penn CNT / epilepsy.science migration)
id: Pennsieve PennEPI* (103 datasets, each with its own 10.26275 DOI)
access_details: open - public Pennsieve Discover datasets under CC BY, downloadable without account via Pennsieve (very large)
quality_note: By far the largest open per-patient epilepsy iEEG+imaging-derivative+outcome collection found outside OpenNeuro/iEEG.org; BIDS-native and outcome-labelled. Limits: terabyte scale, MEF3 format, 103 separate datasets to assemble, SOZ/seizure times not exposed as tabular BIDS annotations in the listings checked, raw MRI/CT only in a minority.
relevance: Core resource for iEEG + MRI structure-function coupling, SOZ/outcome prediction, electrode-to-atlas mapping and normative iEEG work; add diffusion MRI externally for tractography-based coupling. May overlap with the HUP iEEG patients (ds004100), which come from the same Penn programme. Pennsieve lists 103 PennEPI datasets (CC BY, released March 2026), about 19.5 TB in total.
same_subject_data: Yes: each subject bundles iEEG + MNI electrode coordinates with FreeSurfer, ieeg_recon and voxtool_ct derivatives (14 of 14 sampled datasets); raw T1w/CT in the primary folder only in some (2 of 14 sampled had CT, one checked had T1w); no diffusion MRI seen
population: Patients with medication-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing intracranial evaluation at Penn (adult and some pediatric, per participants.json 'population' field)
paper: No dedicated data paper found; datasets authored by Sinha N, Conrad E, Davis K, Wagenaar J, Litt B (Penn CNT), published on Pennsieve Discover 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-09 (BIDS 1.10.1, iEEG-BIDS Migration Tool); cite via epilepsy.science footer
format: BIDS (iEEG as MEF3 directories, NIfTI, FreeSurfer, tsv/json)
size: about 19.5 TB total across 103 datasets (roughly 30-670 GB each, median about 150 GB)
check_note: Added in the 14 Oct 2026 verification pass after reading its record page and paper.

name: HUP iEEG Epilepsy Dataset (Penn / Litt lab)
annotations: SOZ, Seizures, Outcome, Resected contacts, Electrode coords, Clinical data
access_details: open - OpenNeuro, no registration; download by browser, DataLad, openneuro-cli or AWS S3
quality_note: Curated BIDS, ictal + interictal, per-channel SOZ and resection labels, Engel outcomes and MNI coordinates for every patient; best-curated single-center SEEG/ECoG surgical set that is fully open. Lacks raw MRI/CT.
relevance: Core dataset for SOZ / resection / outcome vs functional-connectivity analyses. MNI contact coordinates let you assign contacts to WM vs GM using template atlases or template tractograms, but there is no subject-specific T1/CT/dMRI, so subject-level WM labels and tractography need another source.
same_subject_data: iEEG + MNI electrode coordinates only. No T1/CT/dMRI files in the OpenNeuro release (file listing shows only iEEG, channels, events, electrodes, coordsystem, scans).
population: Drug-resistant focal epilepsy, adults (16-59 y, mean ~34), single center (Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania); implant SEEG 38 / ECoG 20; treated by resection 29 / laser ablation 29; lesional 27 / non-lesional 30; targets mainly temporal, MTL, frontal
paper: Bernabei JM, Li A, Revell AY, et al. 2023, Brain 146(6):2248-2258, doi:10.1093/brain/awad007 (release accompanies this paper); README also cites Kini 2019 Brain (virtual resection) and Bernabei 2022 Brain (normative iEEG maps)
format: BIDS 1.4.0 iEEG; EDF; made with MNE-BIDS; ictal and interictal runs
check_note: OpenNeuro ds004100 snapshot 1.1.3: 57 subjects, 14.2 GB, CC0.
check_changes: added tags Clinical data
confirmed_in_files: HUP: per-contact SOZ and resection flags, Engel outcome, lesion status and age at onset; 213 seizure clips (onset 120 s into each) and two 5-min interictal clips per patient; template coordinates only (fsaverage vs MNI label conflict), no anatomical labels. (checked 12 Oct 2026)

name: MOBILE - Multimodal Whole Brain Imaging in Epilepsy (SEEG + EEG-MEG + 3T/7T MRI incl. dMRI + FDG-PET; patients and healthy controls)
modalities: SEEG, MEG, Scalp EEG, T1, T2, dMRI, rs-fMRI, PET, CT, Post-op MRI, FLAIR, EEG-fMRI
access_details: DUA/application - controlled access: EBRAINS account (free registration) and an explicit data-access request via the EBRAINS data proxy; EBRAINS Data Use Agreement applies (non-commercial use, cite DOI)
quality_note: Exceptional breadth (SEEG, MEG, dMRI at 3T and 7T, PET, spectroscopy) with healthy controls and surgical follow-up MRI; only 30 patients; per-patient outcome (Engel/ILAE) not confirmed from metadata; dataset page itself could not be opened (JS consent banner), metadata taken from DataCite.
relevance: Best public candidate found for same-patient SEEG + dMRI tractography + MEG with an EI-defined epileptogenic zone; contacts can be placed in white/gray matter from CT + 7T MRI. Check outcome/resection labels after obtaining access.
same_subject_data: Yes - in the same 30 patients: SEEG (seizures, rest, sleep) + post-implant CT + EEG-MEG + 3T and 7T MRI (T1w, T2*w, FLAIR, dMRI, rs-fMRI) + 3T MRSI + 7T sodium MRI + FDG-PET (post-surgical 3T T1w in those operated). Controls (32) have EEG-MEG, 3T/7T MRI incl. dMRI and rs-fMRI, 7T sodium and phosphorus MRI and 7T EEG-fMRI whenever feasible; no SEEG in controls
population: 30 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients (median age 31.5, range 17-59, 50% female) undergoing SEEG, plus 32 age-matched healthy controls (median age 28, range 23-39); Marseille (CRMBM, Timone Hospital)
paper: Dary H, Hemmer N, Tilsley P, et al. (27 authors, Marseille: CRMBM/CEMEREM and INS, Timone Hospital; corresponding author Guye M). MOBILE: Multimodal Whole Brain Imaging in Epilepsy, EBRAINS data descriptor v1.1 (released 2026-07-10), doi:10.25493/RPSQ-END. v1.0 (2023-07-05, doi:10.25493/ta4q-34t) had 15 patients and no controls. Related: Wang HE et al. Sci Transl Med 2023 (Delineating epileptogenic networks...); Makhalova J et al. Epilepsia 2022 (VEP modeling, seizure onset and outcome); Azilinon M et al. Hum Brain Mapp 2023 (sodium MRI + MRSI + intracerebral EEG)
format: BIDS v1.7.0 (raw plus derivatives: FreeSurfer with VEP atlas, presurfer, QSM, EI, GARDEL electrode localisation)
size: not stated (large multimodal 7T/3T BIDS release with raw and derivative data)
check_note: DataCite and EBRAINS record confirm 30 patients and 32 controls, controlled access (EBRAINS account plus explicit request, non-commercial Data Use Agreement); descriptor documents SEEG contact labels EZ/PZ/NI from the Epileptogenicity Index, seizure events files and CT-based contact coordinates, but no surgical outcome, resection masks or pathology; first release was v1.0 in 2023.
check_changes: access terms updated; year 2026 → 2023; reference updated; size unverified (large multimodal 7T release) → not stated (large multimodal 7T/3T BIDS release with raw and derivative data); population updated; same-subject data updated; format updated; added modalities FLAIR, EEG-fMRI
confirmed_in_files: MOBILE: SEEG, 64-direction dMRI, connectomes and epileptogenicity-based EZ labels in 30 patients after an EBRAINS access request; outcome labels not documented. (checked 12 Oct 2026)

name: F-TRACT probabilistic CCEP atlas (Zenodo and EBRAINS releases)
access_details: open - Zenodo download (free for research use only, limited accuracy per the record)

name: MNI Open iEEG Atlas (wake) and Multicenter iEEG Sleep Atlas
access_details: Landing page is a LORIS login page (HTTP 401 is just LORIS answering without a session; page is live). It has a 'Request Account' button: you request an account for the atlas dataset and tools; access is for research purposes only, no commercial use without written consent. Downloads of all channels, selected regions or custom selections; high-sampling-rate data for HFO analysis also downloadable. The multicentre sleep atlas (11 sites, 6 countries; BIDS, 24-h and resting recordings with sleep/wake annotation) is on a separate LORIS portal (ieegatlas.loris.ca) whose page could not be read. Contact Dr Birgit Frauscher (MNI).
quality_note: Normative (non-pathological) channels only; no SOZ/outcome information by design.
relevance: Normative iEEG reference for regional electrophysiology; can be paired with normative tractography/connectome atlases for group-level structure-function coupling; not subject-level multimodal.
same_subject_data: iEEG with electrode coordinates in MNI space; individual MRI/dMRI not released (unverified).
population: Wake atlas: 1772 channels with normal activity from 106 subjects (MNI, Grenoble-Alpes University Hospital, CHUM) with drug-resistant focal epilepsy; only channels outside epileptogenic/lesional tissue; filterable by region, electrode type and sleep stage.
paper: Frauscher B et al. Brain 2018;141(4):1130-1144 (doi:10.1093/brain/awy035); Frauscher B et al. High frequency oscillations in the normal human brain. Ann Neurol 2018 (doi:10.1002/ana.25304); von Ellenrieder N et al. How the human brain sleeps: direct cortical recordings from normal human sleep. Ann Neurol 2019 (doi:10.1002/ana.25651)
license: Research use only; no commercial use without written consent (LORIS account required); no standard open licence
format: BIDS iEEG (sleep atlas); atlas channel tables/EDF (wake atlas, unverified)
check_note: Site is live (login page, HTTP 401 is normal); 106 subjects/1772 channels confirmed; access is account request, research-use only, no commercial use.
check_changes: access open → registration; access terms updated; license unverified (no licence text found) → Research use only; no commercial use without written consent (LORIS account required); no standard open licence; reference updated; population updated; quality note updated
confirmed_in_files: MNI Open iEEG Atlas: normative wake and sleep-stage iEEG with MNI coordinates and region labels; download needs an approved account (research-only licence). (checked 12 Oct 2026)

name: STReEF - Structural and effective brain connectivity in focal epilepsy (SPES + DTI-derived structural connectivity)
annotations: Electrode coords, SOZ, Evoked responses, WM/GM labels

access_details: paid - fee-based application through the UK Biobank Access Management System; data are analysed on the UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform (no downloads). Reports from 2026 describe a pause of the platform and of new applications; check the UK Biobank site for the current status before applying.
quality_note: Outstanding acquisition standardisation and sample size, but epilepsy labels are coarse administrative codes with no EEG, semiology, lesion or surgical-outcome data; dMRI is 2 mm multi-shell (tractography feasible but lower resolution than HCP).
relevance: Useful as a large normative/control reference for white-matter tractography and as a population-epilepsy case-control sample (white-matter microstructure, genetics), not for iEEG-vs-tractography coupling. The cheapest route is the £500 student tier.
same_subject_data: Yes by design within imaged participants: T1/FLAIR/SWI/dMRI/rs-fMRI/tfMRI + genetics + linked health records (100,000-scan milestone reported mid-2025; repeat imaging of ~60,000 participants running to ~2029). No EEG/iEEG and no tractography-vs-electrophysiology pairing.
population: Community-dwelling UK adults recruited at age 40-69; epilepsy ascertained from linked hospital inpatient ICD-10 (G40/G41), primary care (subset) and self-report. Late-onset, population-based epilepsy, not a surgical/presurgical cohort.
paper: Littlejohns TJ et al. The UK Biobank imaging enhancement of 100,000 participants: rationale, data collection, management and future directions. Nat Commun 2020;11:2624
license: UK Biobank access conditions / Material Transfer Agreement: research use only, no re-identification, derived results must be returned to UKB, no redistribution
format: NIfTI/DICOM and tabular data on UKB-RAP; ~3,900 imaging-derived phenotypes (IDPs) incl. dMRI tract/skeleton measures; tabular phenotypes
size: multi-petabyte platform; brain imaging data for >100,000 participants (exact size unverified)
check_note: The site blocks scripted access; fee and access facts come from search excerpts of the official pages, and reports of a 2026 pause of the analysis platform could not be confirmed directly. SOZ and surgical outcome do not exist in UK Biobank (epilepsy comes from linked diagnosis codes).

No public data catalogue was found for CHUM, MNI or Sainte-Justine.

same_subject_data: Presurgical patients have iEEG/SEEG plus MRI locally, but no public catalog or dMRI inventory was found.
population: Drug-resistant epilepsy and paediatric epilepsy patients treated at CHUM, MNI-Hospital and CHU Sainte-Justine.
